faqs.question: What is the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 Single Channel Peristaltic Pump used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 handles both precise reagent dosing and fast bulk fluid transfer, making it suited to reactor feed-batch dosing, chemostat operation, and rapid tank filling and emptying.

faqs.question: What flow rate does the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 deliver?
faqs.answer: In single-channel operation the pump delivers 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min, with the exact figure depending on the tubing bore fitted and the speed setting used.

faqs.question: How accurate is the dosing on the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600?
faqs.answer: Control accuracy is +/-0.5% with a precision of +/-2%, and the retraction function further protects accuracy at small dosed volumes by preventing a drop from forming at the tube tip.

faqs.question: What is the retraction function?
faqs.answer: After each pumping run, the drive briefly reverses to pull the tube back and clear the last drop at the tip, which keeps microlitre-scale dosing accurate rather than letting a hanging drop register as an error.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 be automated?
faqs.answer: Yes. RS232 and analogue interfaces, 0 to 10 V or 4 to 20 mA, put speed, direction, and start and stop under external control from a PLC or process system.

faqs.question: Does the pump include the pump head and tubing?
faqs.answer: No. The pump drive is supplied on its own; the pump head and tubing are selected separately to match your flow rate and fluid chemistry, and Inkarp confirms this configuration before quotation.

faqs.question: What is interval dosing?
faqs.answer: Interval dosing lets you set a dosing volume together with a pause time, from 0.1 seconds to 750 hours, so a multi-step dosing sequence runs unattended exactly as programmed.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 and Ultimate 120?
faqs.answer: Both carry the same dosing accuracy, interval dosing, retraction function, and interfaces. The difference is the top-end speed: 600 rpm against a 120 rpm ceiling, which sets the maximum flow rate each variant reaches.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-FLOW Ultimate 600 run continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes. The pump is rated for continuous 24/7 operation, suited to chemostat feed and other processes that cannot pause.

sections.title: Flow rate and dosing accuracy
body: The number on the datasheet is a range; the number that matters is what your specific tubing bore delivers at your specific speed setting. Flow rate on a peristaltic pump is a function of speed and tubing internal diameter together, not speed alone.

At the low end of the 24 to 600 rpm range, a fine-bore tube delivers microlitre-scale dosing with room to spare. At 600 rpm with a wide-bore tube, the same drive moves toward its 4,056 mL/min ceiling for fast fill and empty work.

The +/-0.5% control accuracy holds the drive steady at whichever point on that curve the application sits, and the +/-2% precision figure describes how tightly repeat doses land relative to each other.

body: Not every pump needs to remember a recipe. Some just need to run fast, run reliably, and answer to a signal from elsewhere in the process. The Hei-FLOW Expert 600 is built for that job: 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min across a 24 to 600 rpm range, at +/-0.5% control accuracy, without the programmable dosing layer that a reactor-dosing pump carries.

The turbo button is the feature this tier is built around. One press takes the drive straight to full speed, which is exactly what a tube needs when it's being drained or a vessel needs when the last of a residue has to come out. There's no menu to navigate and no parameter to set, press it, and the pump responds.

External control runs through a single analogue interface, 0 to 10 V or 4 to 20 mA, handling speed, direction, and start/stop. Wire it into a process controller and the pump takes its commands from the system rather than a person standing at the panel.
Direction reverses with a button press, and an optional foot switch frees both hands for the vessel, which matters most when you're filling something and changing containers often.

body: Two things decide how this pump behaves in your process: the speed you set, and the signal your controller sends it.
Flow rate follows speed and tubing bore together, the same as any peristaltic drive, across 24 to 600 rpm and 2.0 to 4,056 mL/min. What's different here is how the drive is told what to do.

There's no stored program to select. The analogue interface takes a continuous voltage or current signal and translates it directly into speed, direction, and start/stop, so the pump does whatever the signal tells it to do, in real time.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-FLOW Core 120 Multi Channel Peristaltic Pump used for?

faqs.question: Can the same pump run both single-channel and multi-channel heads?

faqs.question: What flow rate does the Core 120 Multi deliver?

faqs.question: Does the pump include the pump head and tubing?

body: Eliminate the need to buy separate pumps for single-channel and multi-channel applications. The Hei-FLOW Core 120 Multi uses one drive that accepts either a single-channel or multi-channel pump head, and you simply change the head to match your workflow as application requirements evolve.

It delivers 0.85 to 861 mL/min with a single-channel head, or 0.005 to 364 mL/min per channel with a multi-channel head, depending on the pump head and tubing selected. Speed is controlled across a 10 to 120 rpm range.
Reverse the pumping direction with a single button, no need to remove the tubing or pump head. There is no display or programming required, which keeps day-to-day operation simple and intuitive.

The drive is built with no user-serviceable internal components, for dependable, low-maintenance performance. It suits straightforward fluid transfer and multi-channel dispensing rather than automated dosing or stored programs.

body: The flow rate this pump delivers depends entirely on which head is fitted, and that's the point. One drive, two very different flow profiles.

With a single-channel head, the pump covers 0.85 to 861 mL/min, a wide enough span for most general transfer work. Fit a multi-channel head instead, and the same drive splits its output across several channels, each running 0.005 to 364 mL/min.
That range makes the multi-channel configuration suited to fine, low-volume work spread across parallel lines, where the single-channel head is built for a single, larger flow.

body: The Hei-FLOW Ultimate 120 Multi is built for applications where accurate, repeatable dosing is more important than moving high volumes of liquid. It achieves +/-1% dosing precision with +/-0.5% control accuracy, the highest precision in the Hei-FLOW range.

Use the same drive with either a single-channel or multi-channel pump head to suit different dosing applications. Program and save key parameters, including speed, tubing diameter, flow display, dosing volume, and interval dosing with pauses of up to 750 hours.

Integrate with laboratory software or PLC systems using RS232 and analogue interfaces for automated control of speed, direction, and start/stop functions. The retraction function briefly reverses the pump after each run to minimise droplet formation and improve dosing accuracy.

Operate the pump safely with the optional foot switch, allowing start and stop control from outside a closed exhaust hood. Designed for pharmaceutical, cosmetic, food, and other applications where precise, repeatable dispensing is essential.
Confirmed model: Hei-FLOW Ultimate 120 Multi, P/N 523-52013-00. Also available as the Ultimate 600 at 600 rpm, single-channel only, or as a Standard model, single-channel only.

sections.title: Channel flow and dosing precision
body: Precision here means two things at once: how tightly the drive holds a set speed, and how tightly repeat doses land against each other. This pump is rated +/-0.5% on the first and +/-1% on the second, both tighter than the equivalent 600 rpm Ultimate.
Channel configuration changes what that precision applies to. A single-channel head puts the full 0.36 to 813 mL/min range and the full +/-1% precision behind one flow.

A multi-channel head splits the drive across several channels, each running 0.005 to 329 mL/min at the same precision, which is what makes parallel, validated dosing across multiple lines possible from one instrument.
